title: Reproduction in Lower and Higher Animals
subject: Biology
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: Modes of asexual reproduction in animals: Gemmules, Budding, and Regeneration?
cards.a:
1. Gemmule formation: Internal asexual buds consisting of archaeocytes enclosed in a protective spicule coat; formed during harsh conditions (e.g. Spongilla / freshwater sponge).
2. Budding: External outgrowth that detaches into a new individual (e.g. Hydra).
3. Regeneration: Regrowth of complete organism from body fragment (e.g. Planaria).
cards.hint: Archaeocytes in sponge gemmules are totipotent cells capable of forming any cell type.

cards.q: Histology of Testis: Functions of Seminiferous Tubules, Sertoli Cells, and Leydig Cells?
cards.a:
1. Seminiferous tubules: Lined by germinal epithelium; site of spermatogenesis.
2. Sertoli cells (Nurse cells): Provide nutrition, structural support to developing spermatozoa, secrete ABP (Androgen Binding Protein), and secrete Inhibin (suppresses FSH).
3. Leydig (Interstitial) cells: Located in connective tissue between tubules; synthesize and secrete Androgens (Testosterone).
cards.hint: Cryptorchidism: Failure of testes to descend into scrotum leading to sterility due to high core body temperature.

cards.q: Trace the pathway of sperm transport through male accessory ducts.
cards.a: Seminiferous tubules $\rightarrow$ Rete testis $\rightarrow$ Vasa efferentia (12-20 ciliated ductules) $\rightarrow$ Epididymis (Caput $\rightarrow$ Corpus $\rightarrow$ Cauda: site of physiological sperm maturation and storage) $\rightarrow$ Vas deferens $\rightarrow$ Ejaculatory duct (receives seminal vesicle duct) $\rightarrow$ Urethra.
cards.hint: Vasectomy involves cutting and ligating a small segment of the vas deferens, blocking sperm transport without affecting hormone levels.

cards.q: Functions and secretions of the three male accessory sex glands?
cards.a:
1. Seminal Vesicles (paired, ~60% semen): Alkaline secretion rich in Fructose (energy for sperms), Fibrinogen, and Prostaglandins (stimulate uterine contractions).
2. Prostate Gland (single, ~30% semen): Milky slightly acidic fluid containing Citric acid, Acid phosphatase, and Amylase; activates sperm motility.
3. Cowper's / Bulbourethral Glands (paired): Clear, viscous, alkaline mucus that lubricates the urethra and neutralizes residual urine acidity.
cards.hint: Presence of fructose in female genital tract is forensic proof of sexual intercourse (rape detection).

cards.q: Histology of Ovary: Sequence of Follicular Development?
cards.a: Primordial follicle $\rightarrow$ Primary follicle (primary oocyte surrounded by granulosa cells) $\rightarrow$ Secondary follicle (theca layer develops, antral fluid appears) $\rightarrow$ Tertiary follicle (antrum forms, theca divides into theca interna & externa) $\rightarrow$ Mature Graafian follicle (secondary oocyte surrounded by zona pellucida and corona radiata).
cards.hint: At birth, human ovaries contain ~2 million primary oocytes, reduced to ~40,000 at puberty (follicular atresia).

cards.q: Structure of a mature Graafian Follicle?
cards.a:
1. Outer Theca externa (fibrous) and inner Theca interna (vascular, secretes Estrogen).
2. Membrana granulosa lining the follicular wall.
3. Antrum: Fluid-filled cavity containing Liquor folliculi.
4. Cumulus oophorus (discus proligerus): Granulosa mound holding the secondary oocyte.
5. Oocyte coats: Non-cellular Zona pellucida (glycoprotein) and radially arranged Corona radiata.
cards.hint: The secondary oocyte expelled at ovulation remains arrested at Metaphase II of meiosis.

cards.q: Spermatogenesis: Stages, ploidy levels, and hormone regulation?
cards.a:
1. Multiplication phase: Spermatogonia (2n) divide mitotically.
2. Growth phase: Form Primary spermatocytes (2n).
3. Maturation phase: Meiosis I produces 2 Secondary spermatocytes (n); Meiosis II produces 4 Spermatids (n).
4. Spermiogenesis: Transformation of non-motile round spermatids into flagellated Spermatozoa (n).
Hormones: GnRH $\rightarrow$ LH acts on Leydig cells (Testosterone); FSH acts on Sertoli cells (ABP & Inhibin).
cards.hint: 1 Primary spermatocyte (2n) yields 4 functional spermatozoa (n).

cards.q: Structure of Human Sperm: 4 parts and their specialized features?
cards.a:
1. Head: Contains elongated haploid nucleus and Acrosome (derived from Golgi complex; contains sperm lysins: hyaluronidase and acrosin).
2. Neck: Contains proximal centriole (initiates cleavage) and distal centriole (forms axial filament).
3. Middle piece: Spiral arrangement of mitochondria (Nebenkern) producing ATP for motility.
4. Tail: Long flagellum with 9+2 microtubule axoneme.
cards.hint: Normal human ejaculate is 2-4 mL with 200-300 million sperms; at least 60% must have normal shape and 40% vigorous motility.

cards.q: Oogenesis: How does it differ fundamentally from Spermatogenesis?
cards.a:
1. Oogenesis begins during embryonic development (no new oogonia form after birth).
2. Meiosis I initiates in fetus but is arrested at Diplotene of Prophase I until puberty.
3. Meiotic divisions are unequal, producing 1 large functional Ovum (oocyte) and 2-3 small non-functional Polar bodies.
4. Meiosis II arrests at Metaphase II and completes ONLY when sperm penetrates the egg.
cards.hint: 1 Primary oocyte yields only 1 functional ovum + polar bodies (unlike spermatocyte which yields 4 sperms).

cards.q: Menstrual Cycle: Phase 1 (Menstrual) and Phase 2 (Proliferative / Follicular)?
cards.a:
1. Menstrual Phase (Days 1-5): Breakdown of functional stratum of endometrium due to sharp drop in Progesterone and Estrogen. Bleeding (35-45 mL) contains blood, tissue fluid, and unfertilized ovum.
2. Proliferative Phase (Days 6-13): Driven by FSH; follicles grow in ovary and secrete Estrogen. Estrogen repairs endometrium (thickens to 3-5 mm, glands elongate, vascularity increases).
cards.hint: Withdrawal of progesterone is the immediate trigger causing menstrual bleeding.

cards.q: Menstrual Cycle: Phase 3 (Ovulatory) and Phase 4 (Secretory / Luteal)?
cards.a:
3. Ovulatory Phase (Day 14): LH Surge (rapid LH peak) triggers rupture of Graafian follicle and release of secondary oocyte into pelvic cavity.
4. Secretory / Luteal Phase (Days 15-28): Ruptured follicle converts to yellow Corpus Luteum under LH, secreting high Progesterone. Endometrium becomes secretory (glands coiled, corkscrew-shaped, bed prepared for implantation).
cards.hint: If fertilization fails, corpus luteum degenerates into white scar tissue called Corpus Albicans.

cards.q: Fertilization: Capacitation and Acrosome Reaction mechanism?
cards.a:
1. Capacitation (5-6 hours in female reproductive tract): Removal of cholesterol and acrosomal membrane stabilizing factors; enhances $Ca^{2+}$ influx and sperm motility.
2. Acrosome Reaction: Release of Hyaluronidase (dissolves hyaluronic acid cementing corona radiata) and Corona Penetrating Enzyme + Acrosin/Zona lysin (digests zona pellucida).
cards.hint: Fertilization typically occurs in the Ampulla of the Fallopian tube.

cards.q: Blocks to Polyspermy: Fast block vs Slow block?
cards.a:
1. Fast Block (Electrical): Depolarization of egg plasma membrane from -70 mV to +20 mV via rapid $Na^+$ influx upon first sperm fusion (lasts 1-2 minutes).
2. Slow Block (Cortical Reaction): Influx of $Ca^{2+}$ triggers exocytosis of cortical granules into perivitelline space; enzymes harden the zona pellucida into a fertilization membrane, permanently inactivating ZP3 receptors.
cards.hint: Fast block is transient; slow block (cortical/zona reaction) is permanent and prevents polyspermy.

cards.q: Early Embryonic Cleavage: Morula to Blastocyst?
cards.a:
Cleavage is holoblastic, unequal, and indeterminate.
- Day 3: Solid ball of 16-32 cells resembling mulberry = Morula.
- Day 4-5: Fluid enters forming a central cavity (blastocoel) = Blastocyst.
- Blastocyst consists of an outer protective single layer (Trophoblast $\rightarrow$ forms chorion/placenta) and an Inner Cell Mass (Embryoblast $\rightarrow$ forms embryo proper).
cards.hint: During cleavage, cell number increases while overall embryonic size remains constant (cells become progressively smaller blastomeres).

cards.q: Implantation and Gastrulation: Essential steps and timeline?
cards.a:
Implantation: Blastocyst attaches to uterine endometrium via trophoblastic enzyme lysis around Day 7 and is completely embedded by Day 10.
Gastrulation: Morphogenetic movement of blastomeres transforming blastocyst into a 3-layered embryo (Ectoderm, Mesoderm, Endoderm).
cards.hint: Human embryonic stem cells are derived from the inner cell mass (embryoblast) of the blastocyst.

cards.q: Fate of the 3 Primary Germ Layers: Key tissue derivatives?
cards.a:
1. Ectoderm: Epidermis of skin, hair, nails, nervous system (brain, spinal cord), retina, lens, enamel of teeth, adrenal medulla.
2. Mesoderm: Dermis of skin, muscles, skeleton, circulatory system (heart, blood vessels, blood), kidneys, gonads, adrenal cortex.
3. Endoderm: Gut epithelial lining (GI tract), respiratory tract, liver, pancreas, thyroid, parathyroid, thymus.
cards.hint: Adrenal cortex is mesodermal; adrenal medulla is ectodermal (neuroectoderm) in origin.

cards.q: Human Placenta: Type, structure, and endocrine hormones?
cards.a:
Human placenta is Hemochorial, Metadiscoidal, and Deciduate.
Hormones secreted:
1. hCG (Human Chorionic Gonadotropin): Maintains corpus luteum; basis of urine pregnancy test (Gravindex).
2. hPL (Human Placental Lactogen): Regulates maternal glucose and stimulates mammary glands.
3. Progesterone & Estrogen: Maintain pregnancy and suppress ovulation.
4. Relaxin (secreted by ovary/placenta): Relaxes pubic symphysis for parturition.
cards.hint: hCG, hPL, and relaxin are produced ONLY during pregnancy in human females.

cards.q: Mechanism of Parturition: Fetal Ejection Reflex and Oxytocin?
cards.a:
Parturition is a neuroendocrine reflex:
1. Fully formed fetus and placenta induce mild uterine contractions (Fetal Ejection Reflex).
2. Signals maternal pituitary to release Oxytocin.
3. Oxytocin acts on uterine myometrium, causing stronger contractions $\rightarrow$ more oxytocin release (positive feedback loop) $\rightarrow$ expulsion of baby through birth canal.
cards.hint: Dilation of cervix (Ferguson reflex) increases oxytocin release exponentially until birth.

cards.q: Colostrum: Definition and immunological significance?
cards.a:
The yellowish, thick first milk secreted by mammary glands during the initial 2-3 days postpartum.
Rich in proteins, minerals, and vitamins, but low in fat.
Critically packed with secretory IgA antibodies providing passive natural immunity to the newborn against gut and respiratory infections.
cards.hint: Colostrum contains abundant IgA antibodies; do not confuse with IgG (which crosses placenta).

cards.q: Barrier and Intrauterine Contraceptive Devices (IUDs) with examples?
cards.a:
1. Barriers: Condoms (Nirodh: prevents STDs), Diaphragms, Cervical caps.
2. IUDs (inserted into uterus):
- Non-medicated: Lippes loop (promotes phagocytosis of sperms).
- Copper-releasing: CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375 (Cu ions suppress sperm motility and fertilizing capacity).
- Hormone-releasing: Progestasert, LNG-20 (make uterus unsuitable for implantation and cervix hostile to sperms).
cards.hint: LNG-20 releases levonorgestrel; CuT is the most widely accepted contraceptive method for spacing in India.

cards.q: Oral Contraceptive Pills and Surgical Methods of Birth Control?
cards.a:
Oral Pills: Contain synthetic Progestogen or Estrogen-Progestin combination; inhibit ovulation and alter cervical mucus (e.g. Saheli: non-steroidal, once-a-week pill developed by CDRI Lucknow, containing Centchroman).
Surgical sterilization (Terminal/Permanent):
- Vasectomy: Cutting and ligating vas deferens in males.
- Tubectomy: Cutting and ligating fallopian tubes in females.
cards.hint: Saheli is a Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulator (SERM) with minimal side effects.

cards.q: Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) and Amniocentesis guidelines?
cards.a:
MTP (Induced Abortion): Legalized in India in 1971 with conditions to prevent misuse. Safe up to 12 weeks (1st trimester); requires 2 registered doctors' approval for 12-20 weeks.
Amniocentesis: Prenatal diagnostic test using amniotic fluid to detect fetal chromosomal/genetic disorders (e.g. Down syndrome); legally banned for sex determination under PC-PNDT Act (1994) to curb female foeticide.
cards.hint: Amniotic fluid contains fetal skin cells that can be karyotyped to analyze chromosomal complement.

cards.q: Sexually Transmitted Infections (STIs): Causative agents and characteristics?
cards.a:
1. Syphilis: Treponema pallidum (bacterium); causes painless chancre, skin rash, gumma; treated with penicillin.
2. Gonorrhea: Neisseria gonorrhoeae (bacterium); painful urination, purulent urethral discharge.
3. Genital Herpes: Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV-2); painful blistering ulcers; incurable.
4. Genital Warts: Human Papillomavirus (HPV); benign cauliflower-like growths; linked to cervical cancer.
cards.hint: Hepatitis B, HIV, and Genital Herpes are STIs that cannot be cured with antibiotics.

cards.q: Assisted Reproductive Technologies (ART): IVF, ZIFT, GIFT, and ICSI?
cards.a:
1. IVF-ET (In Vitro Fertilization & Embryo Transfer): Test tube baby; egg and sperm fertilized in lab.
2. ZIFT (Zygote Intra-Fallopian Transfer): Zygote or early embryo up to 8 blastomeres transferred into fallopian tube.
3. IUT (Intra-Uterine Transfer): Embryo with >8 blastomeres transferred directly into uterus.
4. GIFT (Gamete Intra-Fallopian Transfer): Transfer of unfertilized ovum collected from donor into fallopian tube of recipient female.
5. ICSI (Intra-Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection): Single sperm directly injected into ovum cytoplasm.
cards.hint: GIFT does NOT involve in vitro fertilization; fertilization occurs naturally in vivo inside the fallopian tube.

cards.q: MHT-CET Trap: How many sperms and ova are produced from 50 primary spermatocytes and 50 primary oocytes?
cards.a:
1 Primary spermatocyte $\rightarrow$ 4 Sperms $\Rightarrow 50 \times 4 = 200$ Sperms.
1 Primary oocyte $\rightarrow$ 1 functional Ovum (+ 3 polar bodies) $\Rightarrow 50 \times 1 = 50$ Ova.
Total gametes produced = 200 sperms and 50 ova.
cards.hint: Classic MHT-CET numerical! Always distinguish between spermatocytes (x4) and oocytes (x1).
